intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that arthrogryposis multiplex congenita-9 with immunodeficiency (AMC9) is caused by homozygous mutation in the SENP7 gene.

checks.claim: Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita-9 with immunodeficiency (AMC9) is caused by homozygous mutation in the SENP7 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing identified a homozygous stop gain variant in SENP7 c.1474C>T; p.(Gln492*) as the probable aetiology.
checks.explanation: Homozygous SENP7 variant identified as probable cause of the arthrogryposis/immunodeficiency syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita-9 with immunodeficiency (AMC9) is an autosomal recessive lethal disorder characterized by congenital arthrogryposis, absent achievement of developmental milestones, early respiratory failure, and immunodeficiency with neutropenia, hypogammaglobulinemia, and recurrent infections, with death in infancy (Samra et al., 2023; Kobayashi et al., 2024). Prenatal presentation with multiple congenital anomalies, including central nervous system malformations, congenital heart disease, and renal anomalies, and fetal death has also been reported (Saad et al., 2025).

checks.explanation: Biallelic homozygous variants imply recessive inheritance.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of AMC9 in the families reported by Samra et al. (2023), Kobayashi et al. (2024), and Saad et al. (2025) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance, with affected individuals carrying homozygous SENP7 mutations. Kotecha et al. (2025) identified a recessive SENP7 mutation in a consanguineous family.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of AMC9 in the families reported by Samra et al. (2023), Kobayashi et al. (2024), and Saad et al. (2025) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: We performed exome sequencing and segregation studies in a family with several infants presenting with an unidentified syndrome.
checks.explanation: A homozygous variant with segregation in one family suggests recessive inheritance, but the abstract does not explicitly say so; the other families come from other papers.

checks.claim: Affected individuals in the families reported by Samra et al. (2023), Kobayashi et al. (2024), and Saad et al. (2025) carried homozygous SENP7 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing identified a homozygous stop gain variant in SENP7 c.1474C>T; p.(Gln492*) as the probable aetiology.
checks.explanation: Supported for the Samra family; the other families rest on other papers.

checks.claim: Kotecha et al. (2025) identified a recessive SENP7 mutation in a consanguineous family.
checks.evidence_quote: We report a consanguineous family with multiple affected members with AMC and identified a recessive mutation in the highly conserved splice donor site
checks.explanation: The abstract states that a recessive mutation was found in this consanguineous family, and the abstract makes clear the gene is SENP7.

paragraphs.text: In a kindred with 4 infants with AMC9, Samra et al. (2023) identified a homozygous c.1474C-T nonsense mutation in the SENP7 gene, resulting in a gln492-to-ter (Q492X) substitution, by exome sequencing and segregation studies. Fibroblasts from the proband showed decreased SENP7 mRNA expression, and protein expression studies showed significant protein dysregulation in total cell lysates and in the chromatin fraction. Levels of HP1-alpha, different histones, and H3K9me3 were reduced in patient fibroblasts. Samra et al. (2023) suggested that loss of SENP7 leads to reduced heterochromatin condensation and subsequent aberrant gene expression.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous family with lethal arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, Kotecha et al. (2025) identified a recessive mutation in the highly conserved splice donor site of the SENP7 gene, resulting in mis-splicing of the affected exons.

paragraphs.text: In a fetus from a consanguineous Egyptian family with a lethal multiple congenital anomaly syndrome including arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, Saad et al. (2025) identified a homozygous c.745C-T nonsense mutation in the SENP7 gene, resulting in an arg249-to-ter (R249X) substitution, by singleton exome sequencing of fetal DNA. The mutant mRNA was predicted to be degraded by nonsense-mediated decay.

paragraphs.text: Pal et al. (2025) reported a novel missense variant in SENP7 in a patient with fatal arthrogryposis multiplex congenita and immunodeficiency and summarized the clinical and molecular findings in previously reported cases. Details of the variant were not available in the abstract.

checks.explanation: The title states that a novel missense variant in SENP7 was found in fatal AMC with immunodeficiency. The abstract fragment's mention of 'our case' supports the single-patient wording. Details of the variant are not in the supplied text.

agent.process_note: All 5 papers are available only as abstracts, and I read each one in full. The Pal et al. (2025) abstract is a fragment of one sentence, so it does not give the missense variant or any patient details. The Kotecha et al. (2025) abstract does not say exactly what the splice-site variant is or whether it is homozygous. The Kobayashi et al. (2024) abstract does not name its variants. So only Q492X and R249X are listed as allelic variants. No HGNC reference data were supplied, so the intro leaves out SENP7's gene MIM number and chromosome location.
